clue.text: A second reformation for clergy

indicators.note: a reformation re-forms something, so the letters of these two words are made into a new shape

explanation.surface: A second Reformation sweeps through the church's ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformation' tempts with church history, but it asks for A SECOND to be re-formed.
explanation.definitionFit: Deacons are ordained ministers ranking below priests, so they belong to the clergy.

clue.text: Prevent one's speech becoming worse

parts.note: to deter is to prevent or discourage
one gives I, the Roman numeral
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A speaker's address gets steadily worse as it goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Deterioration is decline, the process of worsening.

clue.text: Performer in a European big top?

indicators.note: top means the first letter of big

explanation.surface: A circus act features a European under the big top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big top' wants to be the circus tent; only its top letter B counts.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat is a gymnast who entertains audiences, an artiste.

clue.text: Beginning film here?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the place where a movie is shot is ...

explanation.definitionFit: Onset means start, and split as two words it is where a film is shot.

clue.text: Small container poet provided for fish

parts.note: a tin is a metal container
Thomas Gray wrote the famous Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard

explanation.surface: A poet keeps a little container of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat sea creature with a venomous tail spine.

clue.text: Biblical characters joining many things together

parts.note: Job and Lot are two figures from the Old Testament
Job and Lot are two figures from the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Two Old Testament figures join up in a gathering of many things.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives both pieces: Job, of patient suffering, and Lot, Abraham's nephew.
explanation.definitionFit: A job lot is a mixed batch of items sold together at auction as a single unit.

clue.text: Dances with Wolves — primarily about a problem with fitting in?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first two pieces go around the letter A

parts.note: jigs are lively folk dances

indicators.note: primarily means just the opening letter of Wolves

explanation.surface: Someone watching the film Dances with Wolves struggles to fit in.
explanation.walkthrough: Dances with Wolves is a 1990 film, a decoy title split into JIGS and W.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a puzzle solved by fitting its pieces together.

clue.text: Solution with "dale" erroneously in place of "dole"

indicators.note: in places the jumbled word inside the word for solution

parts.note: brine is a salt solution

indicators.note: erroneously means wrongly, so the letters of dale are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An editor's note about a misprint swapping one word for another.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue poses as a correction note; 'Solution' means salt water, not an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The breadline is the level of poverty at which people depend on state handouts.

clue.text: Chemical causing a reaction in the west, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the Occident is the West, the western world

explanation.surface: A chemical causes a stir in the western world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reaction' suggests public response, but it is the chemical sort.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxidant is a reagent that brings about oxidation in other substances.

clue.text: Article about hasty punishment

indicators.note: about means going around, so the article's word is placed around the other piece

parts.note: an article is a thing, an item
hasty means rash

explanation.surface: A newspaper article criticises a punishment handed down in haste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a grammar word like A or THE, but here it means an object.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrashing is a beating given as a punishment.

clue.text: Girl getting work on newspaper — with a bit of help

parts.note: to edit is to prepare copy for a paper

indicators.note: a bit of means only a small piece, the opening letter, of the word help is used

explanation.surface: A young woman lands a newspaper job with a little assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith is a female first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: Going out? Then view a C a a n movie

indicators.note: going out means leaving its normal arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.words: Then view a C a a n

explanation.surface: Thinking of an evening out, someone suggests watching a film with James Caan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going out' suggests a night out, but it scrambles THEN VIEW A CAAN; the film is from 1978.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven Can Wait is a 1978 Warren Beatty film comedy.

clue.text: Thoughtless worker, British in origin

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for British inside the word for origin

parts.note: an origin is a root, the source of something

explanation.surface: A careless labourer turns out to have British roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British in origin' reads as a nationality, but it puts B into ROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is a machine that labours without thinking.

clue.text: Male relative given sum of money repeatedly each year

parts.note: a grand is a thousand pounds or dollars

indicators.note: repeatedly means the abbreviation for each year is written twice

parts.note: PA is per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: An elderly relative receives an annual sum of money year after year.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandpapa is an old-fashioned name for a grandfather, a male family member.

clue.text: Too plain for modelling — but it's not necessary

indicators.note: modelling means shaping clay, so the letters of the two words are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone too plain to be a model is told looks are not required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modelling' suggests the catwalk, but it means shaping TOO PLAIN anew.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optional is left to choice, so it is not required.

clue.text: Odious attack

definitions.meaning: an attack is a military push, especially a large planned one

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something repugnant and a noun for a military assault.

clue.text: Petty officer accepts italian and French article

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the officer's abbreviation holds the next letter

parts.note: LT is short for lieutenant, an officer
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it
le is the French word for the

explanation.surface: A petty officer takes in an Italian and a French item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petty officer' looks like a naval rank, but Petty is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty means trivial or small, as in small-minded.

clue.text: In the wood, climbing, all fall down

indicators.note: In places the reversed word inside the word for wood

parts.note: a copse is a small wood

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word all is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: Everyone climbing in the woods tumbles down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' means reading upwards, so the word turns round before going into the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse is to give way and drop down.

clue.text: Backing provided by priest in Italian resort

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the whole run of both pieces is read backwards

parts.note: provided means if, on condition that
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: A priest's financial backing supports a seaside resort in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' sounds like sponsorship, but it reverses IF and LAMA together.
explanation.definitionFit: Amalfi is a town on Italy's southern coast, a popular holiday destination.

clue.text: A university attended by FBI agents needing time to grow

parts.note: G-men are American federal agents

explanation.surface: FBI agents enrol at a university and need time to develop.
explanation.walkthrough: G-MEN is US slang for government (FBI) agents.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to increase or enlarge.

clue.text: Jam not finished by head of household

parts.note: dome is slang for a head

indicators.note: not finished means the final letter of the word for jam is dropped

parts.note: to jam is to stick, become stuck

explanation.surface: The head of the household has not got round to making jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of household' reads as one phrase, but head gives DOME and 'of household' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic describes things relating to the home and family life.

clue.text: Historian has been distracted by trifle

parts.note: to toy is to trifle, play idly

indicators.note: distracted means scattered, so the letters of been are mixed

explanation.surface: A historian has lost focus over something trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnold Toynbee was a British historian known for A Study of History.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Toynbee was a celebrated 20th-century scholar of the past.

clue.text: Supporter of half-day closing

indicators.note: half means only half of the weekday's name is kept

parts.note: Friday is a day of the week
an end is a close or conclusion

explanation.surface: Someone backs early closing of the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-day closing is a British custom of shops shutting one afternoon a week.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend is an ally or backer.

clue.text: Nine large nuts, mostly

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of the two words go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Nine big nuts make up most of the mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like a noun here, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In general means usually or for the most part.

clue.text: Attempt to deceive right back over there

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for right is turned round

parts.note: yon is an old word for that place over there

explanation.surface: Someone tries to trick a person by pointing behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: TRY ON is the British informal 'try-on', an attempt to fool someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A try-on is a bluff or trick to see what one can get away with.

clue.text: Pair of trousers revealed for swimmer

indicators.note: pair of means the opening two letters of trousers are taken

parts.note: out means exposed, revealed

explanation.surface: A pair of trousers is exposed for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pair of trousers' reads as clothing; it means the first two letters of trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater fish, a swimmer.

clue.text: No Scottish girl has birthmarks

parts.note: nae is the Scots word for no
Vi is short for the girl's name Violet

explanation.surface: A Scottish girl insists she has no birthmarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No Scottish girl' reads as one phrase, but it splits in two: the Scots word for no, then a short girl's name.

clue.text: Spurge discovered by first of botanists in high state

indicators.note: in places the opening letter of botanists inside the word for high state

explanation.walkthrough: 'High state' suggests altitude or politics, but it means elation.

clue.text: Be there as a nurse, covering patient's back

indicators.note: back means the final letter of patient's

explanation.walkthrough: 'As a nurse' reads as a role, but A gives A and nurse gives TEND, which holds the T.

clue.text: In the centre a tramp appears, as beggars do

indicators.note: In means the answer sits inside the run of words centre a tramp

explanation.surface: A homeless man turns up in the town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Beggars plead or implore passers-by, which is to beseech.
